items.short: How much water a well-watered grass surface would lose to air and plants in a day, set by weather.
ETo times the crop coefficient Kc: how much water the actual crop uses.
A crop-stage multiplier that turns ETo into ETc.
Where today's soil moisture sits compared with the same time of year in past years.
A greenness index from satellite images; low values mean bare soil, high values mean plant cover.
Days when minimum temperature is cold enough to damage a crop that is at a tender stage.
Crop water use minus useful rain and stored soil water; the rest must be irrigated.
How hot the ground and canopy are, seen from space, compared with normal.
Satellite gravity data show regional groundwater change; SGMA is California's groundwater law.
The water a district or GSA lets you use per acre; 1 acre-ft/acre is about 305 mm.
Each dataset has a cell size; a 9 km cell cannot see inside a 60 ha field.
A label is checked ground truth; a pseudo-label is a rule's guess used to train a model.
An unsupervised method that flags weeks that look unusual compared with the rest.
